objects.description: Legacy/basic header information for a file entry inside a RAR archive. Contains ASCII arc and file names, sizes, CRC, timestamps, method, attributes, and optional comment buffer metadata. Packed to 1 byte alignment as per surrounding pragma.

Extended header for RAR file entries with wide-string fields, 64-bit sizes (via High parts), hashing info, redirection metadata, full timestamps, and extended name buffers. Packed to 1 byte alignment.
Parameters and results for opening an archive (ANSI). Caller sets ArcName and OpenMode; library fills OpenResult and optional comment info.

objects.definition: typedef int (CALLBACK *UNRARCALLBACK)(UINT msg,LPARAM UserData,LPARAM P1,LPARAM P2);
objects.description: Function pointer type for the library callback invoked for events such as volume changes, data processing, and password requests. Calling convention may vary per platform macros.

Extended open-archive parameters (supports Unicode names, flags, callback, user data, and optional wide comment buffer/MOTW). Caller initializes inputs; library returns results such as OpenResult and possibly comment data. Packed to 1 byte alignment.

Function pointer type for legacy volume-change callback (ANSI). Library can invoke this when a multi-volume archive needs the next part.
Function pointer type for data-processing callback; called with a buffer and size during extraction or testing.

functions.name: RAROpenArchive
functions.description: Opens a RAR archive for listing or extraction using a narrow (char*) archive name. On success returns an opaque HANDLE to be used with subsequent UNRAR API calls; the result code is also written to ArchiveData->OpenResult. Use RARCloseArchive to close the handle. Typical usage: initialize RAROpenArchiveData, set ArcName and OpenMode (RAR_OM_LIST/RAR_OM_EXTRACT/RAR_OM_LIST_INCSPLIT), optionally provide CmtBuf/CmtBufSize, call RAROpenArchive, check OpenResult, then iterate headers and process files.
requirements: ArchiveData must be a valid, writable pointer to a zero-initialized RAROpenArchiveData structure.
ArchiveData->ArcName must point to a valid, null-terminated path string to the archive to open.
ArchiveData->OpenMode must be set to one of: RAR_OM_LIST, RAR_OM_EXTRACT, or RAR_OM_LIST_INCSPLIT.
If archive comments are desired, ArchiveData->CmtBuf and ArchiveData->CmtBufSize must be set; the buffer must be writable and at least CmtBufSize bytes long.
Caller must check ArchiveData->OpenResult for ERAR_* status after the call.
On success, the returned HANDLE must be closed with RARCloseArchive exactly once.
The returned HANDLE must be passed back only to functions from this API; do not use after RARCloseArchive.

functions.name: RAROpenArchiveEx
functions.description: Extended open for a RAR archive with support for wide-character names, callbacks, and additional flags. Returns a HANDLE for subsequent operations and sets ArchiveData->OpenResult. Supports optional comment buffers in both char* and wchar_t*, and operation flags via OpFlags. Typical usage mirrors RAROpenArchive but with the Ex structure fields; may set Callback and UserData to receive events.
requirements: ArchiveData must be a valid, writable pointer to a zero-initialized RAROpenArchiveDataEx structure.
Either ArchiveData->ArcName (char*) or ArchiveData->ArcNameW (wchar_t*) must point to a valid, null-terminated archive path.
ArchiveData->OpenMode must be set to one of: RAR_OM_LIST, RAR_OM_EXTRACT, or RAR_OM_LIST_INCSPLIT.
If using comment retrieval, set ArchiveData->CmtBuf with CmtBufSize and/or CmtBufW; buffers must be writable and at least the specified size.
If using callbacks at open time, ArchiveData->Callback must be a valid UNRARCALLBACK and ArchiveData->UserData will be passed back unmodified.
ArchiveData->OpFlags may include ROADOF_KEEPBROKEN; other flag values for ArchiveData->Flags are indicated by ROADF_* after open (read-only info).
Caller must check ArchiveData->OpenResult for ERAR_* status after the call.
On success, the returned HANDLE must be closed with RARCloseArchive exactly once.
The returned HANDLE must be used only with this API and becomes invalid after RARCloseArchive.

functions.name: RARCloseArchive
functions.description: Closes an archive handle obtained from RAROpenArchive/RAROpenArchiveEx and releases associated resources. Returns an ERAR_* status code indicating the result of the close operation.
requirements: hArcData must be a HANDLE previously returned by RAROpenArchive or RAROpenArchiveEx.
Each successful open must be matched by exactly one RARCloseArchive call.
Do not use hArcData with any other API after it has been closed.
Caller should check the returned ERAR_* code for success or failure.

functions.name: RARReadHeader
functions.signature: int PASCAL RARReadHeader(HANDLE hArcData, struct RARHeaderData *HeaderData);
functions.description: Reads the next file header from the opened archive and fills a narrow-character RARHeaderData structure with metadata about the item. Typically called in a loop until ERAR_END_ARCHIVE, followed by RARProcessFile to act on each entry.
requirements: hArcData must be a valid archive HANDLE from RAROpenArchive/RAROpenArchiveEx.
HeaderData must be a valid, writable pointer to a RARHeaderData structure.
Call repeatedly to enumerate all entries; stop when ERAR_END_ARCHIVE is returned.
After a successful header read, the next step is to call RARProcessFile with the desired operation for that entry.
Caller should check the returned ERAR_* code; ERAR_SUCCESS indicates a header was read, ERAR_END_ARCHIVE indicates no more entries.

functions.name: RARReadHeaderEx
functions.signature: int PASCAL RARReadHeaderEx(HANDLE hArcData, struct RARHeaderDataEx *HeaderData);
functions.description: Reads the next file header using the extended header structure, providing wide-character names and additional metadata (dictionary size, hash info, timestamps, redirection info, etc.). Used similarly to RARReadHeader but with the Ex structure.
requirements: hArcData must be a valid archive HANDLE from RAROpenArchive/RAROpenArchiveEx.
HeaderData must be a valid, writable pointer to a RARHeaderDataEx structure.
Call repeatedly to enumerate entries; stop when ERAR_END_ARCHIVE is returned.
After a successful header read, process the entry with RARProcessFile or RARProcessFileW as appropriate.
Caller should check the returned ERAR_* code for success or termination.

functions.name: RARProcessFile
functions.signature: int PASCAL RARProcessFile(HANDLE hArcData, int Operation, char *DestPath, char *DestName);
functions.description: Performs an operation on the current entry whose header was read: skip, test, or extract. Uses narrow-character output paths/names. When extracting, DestPath and/or DestName can control the destination; for test and skip they may be unused. Returns an ERAR_* status code.
requirements: hArcData must be a valid archive HANDLE with a header successfully read via RARReadHeader/RARReadHeaderEx.
Operation must be one of: RAR_SKIP, RAR_TEST, or RAR_EXTRACT.
If Operation is RAR_EXTRACT and output is desired to a specific location, DestPath and/or DestName must be valid, null-terminated strings; behavior if NULL is library-defined/unknown.
For RAR_SKIP or RAR_TEST, DestPath and DestName may be NULL (unused).
If the archive is encrypted or the file requires a password, a password must be provided beforehand via RARSetPassword or via a callback (UCM_NEEDPASSWORD/UCM_NEEDPASSWORDW).
Caller should check the returned ERAR_* code for success or failure of the operation.

functions.name: RARProcessFileW
functions.signature: int PASCAL RARProcessFileW(HANDLE hArcData, int Operation, wchar_t *DestPath, wchar_t *DestName);
functions.description: Wide-character variant of RARProcessFile. Performs skip, test, or extract on the current entry, using wchar_t for destination path and name. Returns an ERAR_* status code.
requirements: hArcData must be a valid archive HANDLE with a header successfully read via RARReadHeader/RARReadHeaderEx.
Operation must be one of: RAR_SKIP, RAR_TEST, or RAR_EXTRACT.
If Operation is RAR_EXTRACT and a specific destination is required, DestPath and/or DestName must be valid, null-terminated wide strings; behavior if NULL is library-defined/unknown.
For RAR_SKIP or RAR_TEST, DestPath and DestName may be NULL (unused).
If a password is required, set it beforehand using RARSetPassword (narrow) or rely on callbacks (UCM_NEEDPASSWORDW).
Caller should check the returned ERAR_* code for operation result.

functions.name: RARSetCallback
functions.signature: void PASCAL RARSetCallback(HANDLE hArcData, UNRARCALLBACK Callback, LPARAM UserData);
functions.description: Registers or clears a general callback for archive events on the given handle. The callback receives messages defined in UNRARCALLBACK_MESSAGES (e.g., UCM_CHANGEVOLUME, UCM_PROCESSDATA, UCM_NEEDPASSWORD and their wide variants, UCM_LARGEDICT). UserData is passed back to the callback in each invocation.
requirements: hArcData must be a valid archive HANDLE from RAROpenArchive/RAROpenArchiveEx.
Callback must conform to the UNRARCALLBACK type: int CALLBACK f(UINT msg, LPARAM UserData, LPARAM P1, LPARAM P2). Pass NULL to disable callbacks.
UserData can be any value; it is passed unmodified to the callback.
Callback code must handle only the documented message IDs in UNRARCALLBACK_MESSAGES; other values should be treated as unknown/unsupported.
Set the callback before operations that may trigger callbacks (e.g., before reading headers or processing files).

functions.name: RARSetChangeVolProc
functions.signature: void PASCAL RARSetChangeVolProc(HANDLE hArcData, CHANGEVOLPROC ChangeVolProc);
functions.description: Registers or clears a legacy change-volume callback using a narrow-character function pointer. The callback is invoked when the library needs to switch volumes for multi-part archives.
requirements: hArcData must be a valid archive HANDLE from RAROpenArchive/RAROpenArchiveEx.
ChangeVolProc must match the typedef: int PASCAL f(char *ArcName, int Mode). Pass NULL to disable.
Register the callback before operations that may require changing volumes.

functions.name: RARSetProcessDataProc
functions.signature: void PASCAL RARSetProcessDataProc(HANDLE hArcData, PROCESSDATAPROC ProcessDataProc);
functions.description: Registers or clears a legacy process-data callback which is invoked as data is processed. Useful for progress tracking or custom handling. Uses a narrow-character callback signature.
requirements: hArcData must be a valid archive HANDLE from RAROpenArchive/RAROpenArchiveEx.
ProcessDataProc must match the typedef: int PASCAL f(unsigned char *Addr, int Size). Pass NULL to disable.
Register the callback before invoking operations that process data (e.g., RARProcessFile).

functions.name: RARSetPassword
functions.description: Sets (or clears) the password for encrypted archives on the given handle using a narrow, null-terminated string. The password will be used for subsequent header reads and file processing that require it.
requirements: hArcData must be a valid archive HANDLE from RAROpenArchive/RAROpenArchiveEx.
Password must be a valid, null-terminated char* string; pass NULL to clear the current password (behavior for NULL otherwise is library-defined/unknown).
Call before attempting to read encrypted headers or extract/test encrypted files.

functions.name: RARGetDllVersion
functions.description: Returns the UNRAR DLL interface version as an integer. The header defines RAR_DLL_VERSION as 9, which indicates the expected interface level.
requirements: No parameters; may be called at any time to detect the DLL interface version.
Caller should compare the returned value to RAR_DLL_VERSION to ensure compatibility.

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator produces valid filesystem path strings (narrow, null-terminated)
# to be consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() and FUZZ_PARAM_STR() in the provided
# fuzzer stubs for the UNRAR API. The stubs primarily need:
# - A valid archive path for RAROpenArchive / RAROpenArchiveEx
# - Optional comment buffers (arbitrary bytes OK) and destination path/name strings
# The most impactful valid input is a real RAR archive path. Since we cannot do I/O
# or create files here, we instead generate a plausible path string that the harness
# may map to an existing fuzz-provided file. We craft diverse, realistic paths that
# are valid across platforms, including Windows and POSIX styles, and include a
# .rar or .r00 extension to encourage archive recognition.

# Encoding: ANSI (bytes) with a trailing NUL. Limit to <= 4096 bytes total.

WINDOWS_SEPARATORS = ['\\\\', '\\']
POSIX_SEPARATOR = '/'

RAR_EXTS = [
    '.rar', '.RAR', '.RaR',
    '.r00', '.r01', '.r99',
]

DRIVES = [
    'C:', 'D:', 'E:', 'Z:'
]

UNC_HOSTS = [
    'server', 'files', 'nas', 'localhost'
]

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + '._- '

def _rand(rng: random.Random, seq: List[str]):
    return seq[rng.randrange(0, len(seq))]

def _rand_component(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=16) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Include some unicode-ish bytes mapped to ANSI by replacing with ascii fallbacks
    # since we must emit narrow bytes; keep it filesystem-safe
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n))
    # Avoid reserved Windows names occasionally by prefixing/ suffixing
    if s.upper() in {'CON','PRN','AUX','NUL','COM1','LPT1'}:
        s = '_' + s
    # Trim trailing spaces/dots for Windows compliance sometimes
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        s = s.rstrip(' .') or 'x'
    return s

def _build_posix_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    parts = []
    depth = rng.randint(0, 4)
    for _ in range(depth):
        parts.append(_rand_component(rng))
    base = _rand_component(rng, 3, 12)
    ext = _rand(rng, RAR_EXTS)
    parts.append(base + ext)
    prefix = '/' if rng.random() < 0.7 else ''  # absolute or relative
    return prefix + '/'.join(parts)

def _build_windows_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose between drive path and UNC path
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        drive = _rand(rng, DRIVES)
        sep = '\\'
        parts = []
        depth = rng.randint(0, 4)
        for _ in range(depth):
            parts.append(_rand_component(rng))
        base = _rand_component(rng, 3, 12)
        ext = _rand(rng, RAR_EXTS)
        parts.append(base + ext)
        return f"{drive}\\" + "\\".join(parts)
    else:
        host = _rand(rng, UNC_HOSTS)
        share = _rand_component(rng, 3, 10)
        parts = []
        depth = rng.randint(0, 3)
        for _ in range(depth):
            parts.append(_rand_component(rng))
        base = _rand_component(rng, 3, 12)
        ext = _rand(rng, RAR_EXTS)
        parts.append(base + ext)
        return f"\\\\{host}\\{share}\\" + "\\".join(parts)

def _maybe_temp_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Some harnesses place the fuzz file in temp dirs; mimic common patterns
    candidates = [
        '/tmp', '/var/tmp', '/dev/shm',
        'C:\\Temp', 'C:\\Windows\\Temp',
        '.']
    base_dir = _rand(rng, candidates)
    leaf = 'seed_' + ''.join(rng.choice(string.hexdigits.lower()) for _ in range(8))
    ext = _rand(rng, RAR_EXTS)
    sep = '/' if '/' in base_dir else '\\' if '\\' in base_dir else '/'
    return base_dir.rstrip('/\\') + sep + leaf + ext

def _path_variants(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    out: List[bytes] = []
    builders = [_build_posix_path, _build_windows_path]
    # Generate a handful of diverse candidates
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 6)):
        b = _rand(rng, builders)(rng)
        out.append((b + '\x00').encode('utf-8', errors='ignore'))
    # Include a temp-like path
    out.append((_maybe_temp_like(rng) + '\x00').encode('utf-8', errors='ignore'))
    # Include simple relative names
    out.append(((_rand_component(rng,3,10) + _rand(rng, RAR_EXTS)) + '\x00').encode('utf-8', errors='ignore'))
    return out

def _pack_variants_blobs(rng: random.Random, blobs: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Concatenate with NUL separators so FUZZ_PARAM_STR can also pick up pieces
    # Keep under 4096 bytes
    rng.shuffle(blobs)
    buf = b''
    for b in blobs:
        if len(buf) + len(b) + 1 > 4000:
            break
        buf += b
        # add some additional small strings that can serve as comment buffers or dest paths
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            extra = _rand_component(rng, 1, 12).encode('utf-8') + b'\x00'
            if len(buf) + len(extra) <= 4000:
                buf += extra
    return buf

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    blobs = _path_variants(rng)
    # Also include a few plausible destination directories/names for RARProcessFile
    dir_like = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            d = _build_posix_path(rng)
            d = os.path.dirname(d) or '.'
        else:
            d = _build_windows_path(rng)
            d = os.path.dirname(d) or '.'
        dir_like.append((d + '\x00').encode('utf-8', errors='ignore'))
    blobs.extend(dir_like)
    # Include some comment-like buffers (arbitrary bytes but printable)
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 4)):
        n = rng.randint(8, 64)
        s = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n))
        blobs.append((s + '\x00').encode('utf-8', errors='ignore'))
    return _pack_variants_blobs(rng, blobs)

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

def _crc32(data: bytes) -> int:
    import zlib
    return zlib.crc32(data) & 0xFFFFFFFF

# --- RAR4 builder (old format) ---
# RAR4 signature block: 0x52 61 72 21 1A 07 00
# Then follows a sequence of blocks with header CRC and type.
# We'll build a minimal Main Header and one File Header with stored data (no compression).

RAR4_SIG = b"Rar!\x1A\x07\x00"

# RAR4 block types
RAR4_BT_MAIN = 0x73
RAR4_BT_FILE = 0x74

# Main header flags (subset)
MHD_VOLUME      = 0x0001
MHD_COMMENT     = 0x0002
MHD_LOCK        = 0x0004
MHD_SOLID       = 0x0008
MHD_PROTECT     = 0x0010
MHD_PASSWORD    = 0x0020
MHD_FIRSTVOLUME = 0x0040
MHD_ENCRYPTVER  = 0x0080

# File header flags (subset)
LHD_SPLIT_BEFORE = 0x0001
LHD_SPLIT_AFTER  = 0x0002
LHD_PASSWORD     = 0x0004
LHD_COMMENT      = 0x0008
LHD_SOLID        = 0x0010
LHD_LARGE        = 0x0100
LHD_UNICODE      = 0x0200
LHD_SALT         = 0x0400
LHD_EXTTIME      = 0x1000


def _rar4_add_block(block_type: int, flags: int, header_data: bytes, add_data: bytes = b"") -> bytes:
    # RAR4 block header: CRC16(2) | Type(1) | Flags(2) | HeaderSize(2) | [AddSize(4 if flags & 0x8000)] | header_data
    # Header CRC is calculated over bytes starting at Type to end of header (excluding the CRC field itself).
    tmp = bytearray()
    tmp += struct.pack("<B", block_type)
    tmp += struct.pack("<H", flags)
    header_size = 7 + len(header_data)  # base header fields (Type+Flags+HdrSize = 5) + CRC(2) not counted in size field
    if flags & 0x8000:
        header_size += 4
    tmp += struct.pack("<H", header_size)
    if flags & 0x8000:
        tmp += struct.pack("<I", len(add_data))
    tmp += header_data
    crc = _rar4_crc16(tmp)
    header = struct.pack("<H", crc) + bytes(tmp)
    return header + add_data

# RAR4 CRC16 (CRC-16-IBM/ARC polynomial 0xA001)

def _rar4_crc16(data: bytes) -> int:
    crc = 0xFFFF
    for b in data:
        crc ^= b
        for _ in range(8):
            if crc & 1:
                crc = (crc >> 1) ^ 0xA001
            else:
                crc >>= 1
    return crc & 0xFFFF


def build_rar4(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    out = bytearray()
    out += RAR4_SIG

    # Main header: minimal reserved fields
    mh_flags = MHD_FIRSTVOLUME
    if rnd.choice([True, False]):
        mh_flags |= MHD_SOLID
    header_data = struct.pack("<HI", 0, 0)  # Reserved1(2), Reserved2(4)
    out += _rar4_add_block(RAR4_BT_MAIN, mh_flags, header_data)

    # One stored file
    filename_choices = [
        "readme.txt",
        "unicodé.txt",
        "dir/sub/file.bin",
        "零.dat",
    ]
    name = rnd.choice(filename_choices)
    use_unicode = rnd.choice([True, False])
    name_bytes = (name.encode('utf-8', 'ignore') if use_unicode
                  else name.encode('latin-1', 'ignore'))

    file_data = os.urandom(rnd.randint(0, 128))
    pack_size = len(file_data)
    unp_size = len(file_data)
    host_os = 2  # Win32
    file_crc = _crc32(file_data)
    file_time = 0
    unp_ver = 20  # minimum
    method = 0x30  # stored
    file_attr = 0x20  # archive attr

    f_flags = 0x8000  # include AddSize
    if use_unicode:
        f_flags |= LHD_UNICODE

    name_len = len(name_bytes)

    # File header fixed fields layout:
    # <I I B I I B B H I
    # PackSize, UnpSize, HostOS, FileCRC, FileTime, UnpVer, Method, NameSize, FileAttr
    fh_fixed = struct.pack(
        "<IIBIIBBHI",
        pack_size,
        unp_size,
        host_os,
        file_crc,
        file_time,
        unp_ver,
        method,
        name_len,
        file_attr,
    )
    header_data = fh_fixed + name_bytes

    out += _rar4_add_block(RAR4_BT_FILE, f_flags, header_data, file_data)
    return bytes(out)

# --- RAR5 minimal builder ---
RAR5_SIG = b"Rar!\x1A\x07\x01\x00"

# Helper for RAR5 unsigned varint (LEB128-like)

def _uvarint(v: int) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    while True:
        b = v & 0x7F
        v >>= 7
        if v:
            out.append(0x80 | b)
        else:
            out.append(b)
            break
    return bytes(out)

RAR5_BT_MAIN = 1
RAR5_BT_FILE = 2


def build_rar5(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random((seed ^ 0x9E3779B9) & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    out = bytearray()
    out += RAR5_SIG

    # Main header: flags=0, no extra, no data
    main_header = bytearray()
    main_header += _uvarint(RAR5_BT_MAIN)
    main_header += _uvarint(0)  # flags
    main_header += _uvarint(0)  # extra size
    main_header += _uvarint(0)  # data size
    out += main_header

    # File header minimal with stored data
    fname = rnd.choice(["a.txt", "b/inner.bin", "unicodé.txt", "零.dat"]).encode('utf-8')
    data = os.urandom(rnd.randint(0, 128))
    unp_size = len(data)

    fh = bytearray()
    fh += _uvarint(RAR5_BT_FILE)
    fh += _uvarint(0)            # flags
    fh += _uvarint(0)            # extra size
    fh += _uvarint(unp_size)     # data size (stored)

    # File-specific area
    file_hdr = bytearray()
    file_hdr += _uvarint(0)          # file flags
    file_hdr += _uvarint(unp_size)   # UnpSize
    file_hdr += _uvarint(0x20)       # Attrs
    file_hdr += _uvarint(len(fname)) # Name length
    file_hdr += fname

    fh += file_hdr

    out += fh
    out += data
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    if rnd.choice([True, False]):
        buf = build_rar4(seed)
    else:
        buf = build_rar5(seed)
    if len(buf) > 4096:
        buf = buf[:4096]
    return buf

import os
import random
import struct
import zlib

# We want to generate a valid RAR archive (or at least something the UNRAR API can open)
# However, crafting full valid RAR is complex. The fuzz harness passes a filename for a temp file
# containing random data which is then opened by RAROpenArchive/Ex. To exercise successful paths,
# we should emit valid RAR signatures with minimal structures so the library can recognize
# an archive and proceed further. We'll build small RAR archives for RAR 4.x ("Rar!\x1A\x07\x00")
# and RAR 5.0 ("Rar!\x1A\x07\x01\x00"). We'll alternate and include variations such as comment
# areas and simple file entries. These should be small and self-contained.
#
# Notes:
# - RAR5 has a defined header format with sizes and CRCs; we'll construct a minimal archive
#   with a single file entry using STORE (no compression), which UNRAR can list/test.
# - RAR4 (legacy) also can be built minimally: marker header + archive header + file header + data + end.
#   We'll compute header CRCs according to RAR 2.9/3.x spec where possible.
# - To keep complexity bounded and sizes small, we implement a best-effort approximate writer for both.
#   Many UNRAR builds are forgiving on fields like OS/attributes. The goal is validity sufficient to open.
#
# If construction fails, we fallback to emitting just the RAR signatures which often suffice for open.

# Utility: little-endian packers
le16 = lambda x: struct.pack('<H', x & 0xFFFF)
le32 = lambda x: struct.pack('<I', x & 0xFFFFFFFF)
le64 = lambda x: struct.pack('<Q', x & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)


def crc32_le(data: bytes) -> int:
    return zlib.crc32(data) & 0xFFFFFFFF


def rar4_build_single_file(name: str, payload: bytes, add_comment: bool) -> bytes:
    # RAR 4.x signature
    out = bytearray(b"Rar!\x1A\x07\x00")

    # Helper to build a RAR 3.x header with CRC
    def build_header(h_type: int, flags: int, body: bytes) -> bytes:
        # HEAD_CRC (2), HEAD_TYPE (1), HEAD_FLAGS (2), HEAD_SIZE (2), ADD_SIZE (optional) + BODY
        base = bytearray()
        base += b"\x00\x00"  # placeholder CRC
        base += bytes([h_type])
        base += le16(flags)
        head_size = 7  # without ADD_SIZE and body
        header = bytearray()
        header += base
        if flags & 0x8000:  # LONG_BLOCK => include ADD_SIZE
            header += le32(len(body))
            head_total = head_size + 4
        else:
            head_total = head_size
        header += le16(head_total)
        # Now the body follows (for LONG_BLOCK, body size is in ADD_SIZE)
        header += body
        # CRC is computed over header bytes starting at HEAD_TYPE (i.e., excluding CRC field)
        crc = crc32_le(bytes(header[2:])) & 0xFFFF
        header[0:2] = le16(crc)
        return bytes(header)

    # Main archive header (type 0x73), minimal
    MHD_VOLUME = 0x0001
    MHD_COMMENT = 0x0002
    MHD_LOCK    = 0x0004
    MHD_SOLID   = 0x0008
    MHD_NEWNUMBERING = 0x0010
    MHD_AV      = 0x0020
    MHD_PROTECT = 0x0040
    MHD_PASSWORD= 0x0080
    MHD_FIRSTVOLUME=0x0100
    MHD_ENCRYPTVER=0x0200
    LONG_BLOCK=0x8000

    mh_flags = MHD_FIRSTVOLUME
    body = bytearray()
    # HIGH_POSAV (2 bytes), PosAV (4 bytes) for AV info when MHD_AV; we'll skip
    # RAR 2.x/3.x main header body may include reserved bytes; we keep empty.
    out += build_header(0x73, mh_flags, bytes(body))

    # Optional comment (main comment) block (type 0x75). We'll omit for simplicity.
    # Build a file header (type 0x74)
    FHD_SPLIT_BEFORE=0x0001
    FHD_SPLIT_AFTER =0x0002
    FHD_PASSWORD    =0x0004
    FHD_COMMENT     =0x0008
    FHD_SOLID       =0x0010
    FHD_LARGE       =0x0100
    f_flags = 0
    comp_method = 0x30  # 0x30 = STORE
    host_os = 0x00      # MS-DOS/Windows

    file_name_bytes = name.encode('utf-8')[:255]
    name_size = len(file_name_bytes)
    unp_size = len(payload) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    pack_size = unp_size  # since STORE
    file_crc = crc32_le(payload)
    file_time = 0  # DOS time; leave zero
    unp_ver = 15   # minimal
    file_attr = 0x20  # archive attribute

    # If sizes exceed 32-bit, set LARGE and supply high dwords; we keep small
    body = bytearray()
    body += le32(pack_size)
    body += le32(unp_size)
    body += bytes([host_os])
    body += bytes([comp_method])
    body += le32(file_time)
    body += le32(file_crc)
    body += bytes([unp_ver])
    body += bytes([0])  # name encoding (0 = ANSI), we still put UTF-8 bytes
    body += le16(name_size)
    body += le32(file_attr)
    body += file_name_bytes
    # No extended fields since not LARGE/COMMENT

    # Mark block as LONG_BLOCK so ADD_SIZE = data size follows the header
    out += build_header(0x74, LONG_BLOCK | f_flags, bytes(body) + payload)

    # End of archive comment block (0x7B) optional; omit
    return bytes(out)


def rar5_build_single_file(name: str, payload: bytes, add_comment: bool) -> bytes:
    # RAR5 signature with zeroed 2 bytes at end
    out = bytearray(b"Rar!\x1A\x07\x01\x00")

    # RAR5 blocks: [size varint][type varint][flags varint][extra area][data area]
    # We'll implement minimal MAIN and FILE block with STORE method. Checksums are optional via flag.

    def varint(n: int) -> bytes:
        # RAR5 LEB128-like 7-bit chunks, MSB=1 for continuation
        b = bytearray()
        while True:
            c = n & 0x7F
            n >>= 7
            if n:
                b.append(c | 0x80)
            else:
                b.append(c)
                break
        return bytes(b)

    def build_block(btype: int, flags: int, extra: bytes, data: bytes) -> bytes:
        header = bytearray()
        header += varint(btype)
        header += varint(flags)
        header += extra
        size = len(header) + len(data)
        return varint(size) + bytes(header) + data

    # MAIN block (type=1). Flags 0 (no extra fields)
    out += build_block(1, 0, b"", b"")

    # FILE block (type=2)
    # FILE block extra fields can include NAME and SIZE. We'll encode minimal fields in extra area:
    # Subfield: file name (type 0x01), content is UTF-8 name
    name_bytes = name.encode('utf-8')[:255]

    def subfield(ftype: int, content: bytes) -> bytes:
        return varint(ftype) + varint(len(content)) + content

    extra = bytearray()
    extra += subfield(1, name_bytes)

    # Data area: we must include unpacked size and attributes in header fields encoded via flags
    # In RAR5, FILE block uses flags bits to indicate presence of fields in extra area. To simplify,
    # set flags to 0 meaning default regular file, and include required sizes in extra subfields:
    # However spec prefers SIZE subfield (type 2) containing unpacked size and attributes fields.
    unpacked_size = len(payload)
    extra += subfield(2, varint(unpacked_size))

    # Method: 0 = STORE, encoded in extra subfield type 3 (optional). We'll include it.
    extra += subfield(3, varint(0))

    # CRC32 subfield type 4
    extra += subfield(4, le32(crc32_le(payload)))

    file_block = build_block(2, 0, bytes(extra), payload)
    out += file_block

    return bytes(out)


def pick_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    choices = [
        'a.txt',
        'empty',
        'nested/path/file.bin',
        'unicodé-名.txt',
        'longname_' + ('x' * rng.randint(1, 60)) + '.dat',
    ]
    return rng.choice(choices)


def make_payload(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    kind = rng.randrange(4)
    if kind == 0:
        return b''
    elif kind == 1:
        # small text
        text = ('Hello RAR!\n' * rng.randint(1, 50)).encode('utf-8')
        return text[:1024]
    elif kind == 2:
        # patterned binary
        size = rng.randint(1, 2048)
        block = bytes([rng.randrange(256) for _ in range(16)])
        return (block * ((size + 15)//16))[:size]
    else:
        # incremental bytes
        size = rng.randint(1, 2048)
        return bytes((i % 256 for i in range(size)))


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    name = pick_name(rng)
    payload = make_payload(rng)
    add_comment = rng.choice([False, True])

    try_order = []
    if rng.choice([True, False]):
        try_order = ['rar5', 'rar4']
    else:
        try_order = ['rar4', 'rar5']

    for kind in try_order:
        try:
            if kind == 'rar4':
                data = rar4_build_single_file(name, payload, add_comment)
            else:
                data = rar5_build_single_file(name, payload, add_comment)
            if len(data) <= 4096:
                return data
            else:
                return data[:4096]
        except Exception:
            continue

    # Fallback minimal signatures to let the library at least detect format
    if rng.choice([True, False]):
        return b"Rar!\x1A\x07\x01\x00"  # RAR5 marker
    else:
        return b"Rar!\x1A\x07\x00"  # RAR4 marker

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for a valid password string buffer for UNRAR RARSetPassword fuzz stub.
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumes a single contiguous byte buffer and interprets it as a std::string.
# Our task: produce interesting, but valid password strings (null-terminated not required for std::string),
# up to 256 bytes (stub truncates beyond that). We keep overall buffer <= 4096 bytes.
# We bias towards realistic and edge-case passwords: ASCII, Unicode-like UTF-8, long lengths,
# boundary sizes (0, 1, 255, 256), and include common special chars and binary bytes.

SPECIALS = "!@#$%^&*()-_=+[]{};:'\",.<>/?`~|\\"
PRINTABLE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + SPECIALS + " "

COMMON_PASSWORDS = [
    "",  # empty -> clears password
    "password",
    "123456",
    "letmein",
    "admin",
    "toor",
    "qwerty",
    "iloveyou",
    "dragon",
    "monkey",
    # with punctuation
    "P@ssw0rd!",
    "CorrectHorseBatteryStaple",
    # unicode-like sequences (UTF-8)
    "пароль",           # Russian
    "密碼",              # Chinese Traditional
    "كلمةالسر",          # Arabic
    "senha",
    "contraseña",       # Spanish with tilde
    "mot_de_passe",
    "pässwörd",         # Latin-1 like
    "🔐🔑",             # emojis
    # path-like or typical archive-related
    "archive2025",
    "backup-2021-12",
]

# Some UTF-8 sequences to mix in
UNICODE_FRAGMENTS = [
    "ä", "ö", "ü", "ß", "é", "è", "ê", "ñ", "ø", "å",
    "€", "£", "¥", "©", "®", "™",
    "😀", "😁", "😂", "😎", "🗜️", "📦", "🧩",
]

# Binary byte sets for edge cases
BINARY_SETS: List[bytes] = [
    bytes([0x00] * 8),           # NULs (though std::string supports embedded NUL)
    bytes(range(0x00, 0x20)),    # C0 control chars
    bytes(range(0x7F, 0x90)),    # DEL and nearby
]


def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    return ''.join(r.choice(PRINTABLE_ASCII) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_utf8(r: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    # Create a UTF-8 oriented string mixing ASCII and chosen unicode fragments
    out = []
    while len(''.join(out).encode('utf-8')) < n:
        if r.random() < 0.7:
            out.append(r.choice(PRINTABLE_ASCII))
        else:
            out.append(r.choice(UNICODE_FRAGMENTS))
    s = ''.join(out)
    # Trim to desired byte length without breaking UTF-8
    b = s.encode('utf-8')
    return b[:n].decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')


def _biased_lengths(r: random.Random) -> int:
    # Bias towards interesting lengths respecting stub cap (256)
    choices = [0, 1, 2, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 254, 255, 256]
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        return r.choice(choices)
    return r.randint(0, 256)


def _build_candidate(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    mode = r.choices(
        population=[
            'empty', 'common', 'ascii', 'utf8', 'binary', 'pattern', 'repeat', 'mixed'
        ],
        weights=[5, 10, 20, 20, 10, 10, 15, 10],
        k=1
    )[0]

    if mode == 'empty':
        s = ""
        return s.encode('utf-8')

    if mode == 'common':
        s = r.choice(COMMON_PASSWORDS)
        # Optionally append a year or symbol
        if r.random() < 0.4:
            s += str(r.randint(1980, 2035))
        if r.random() < 0.3:
            s += r.choice("!$#@")
        return s.encode('utf-8')[:256]

    if mode == 'ascii':
        n = _biased_lengths(r)
        s = _rand_ascii(r, n)
        return s.encode('ascii')[:256]

    if mode == 'utf8':
        n = _biased_lengths(r)
        s = _rand_utf8(r, n)
        return s.encode('utf-8')[:256]

    if mode == 'binary':
        # Choose from predefined binary sets or random bytes
        if r.random() < 0.6:
            b = bytearray(r.choice(BINARY_SETS))
            # Maybe pad/trim to an interesting length
            target = _biased_lengths(r)
            while len(b) < target:
                b.extend(r.choice(BINARY_SETS))
            return bytes(b[:min(target, 256)])
        else:
            n = _biased_lengths(r)
            b = bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))
            return b[:256]

    if mode == 'pattern':
        # Structured patterns like alternating cases and digits/symbols
        base = []
        n = _biased_lengths(r)
        patterns = ["Aa0!", "aA1#", "Zz9$", "pP2@", "xX3%"]
        pat = r.choice(patterns)
        for i in range(n):
            base.append(pat[i % len(pat)])
        return ("".join(base)).encode('ascii')[:256]

    if mode == 'repeat':
        token = r.choice([
            "a", "A", "0", "!", "Pa", "🔐", "ä", "\x00",
        ])
        # Ensure token is bytes-safe; handle \x00 literal
        if token == "\x00":
            tok_b = b"\x00"
        else:
            tok_b = token.encode('utf-8')
        n = _biased_lengths(r)
        b = tok_b * (max(1, n // max(1, len(tok_b))) )
        return b[:256]

    # mixed
    n = _biased_lengths(r)
    chunks: List[bytes] = []
    while sum(len(c) for c in chunks) < n:
        choice = r.random()
        if choice < 0.4:
            chunks.append(_rand_ascii(r, r.randint(1, 12)).encode('ascii'))
        elif choice < 0.75:
            frag = r.choice(UNICODE_FRAGMENTS).encode('utf-8')
            chunks.append(frag)
        else:
            # occasional binary byte including NUL
            chunks.append(bytes([r.randint(0, 255)]))
    b = b''.join(chunks)[:256]
    return b


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Produce a single password string buffer (FUZZ_PARAM_STR). The harness will
    # read exactly one parameter for RARSetPassword stub.
    buf = _build_candidate(r)
    # Ensure buffer length <= 4096 and not exceeding stub cap (already ≤256)
    if len(buf) > 4096:
        buf = buf[:4096]
    return buf
